clue.text: Cocky's got his own cover, it seems

definitions.text: got his own cover, it seems
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: insured (assured) by oneself rather than by an insurance company

explanation.surface: Someone cocky has taken out a policy on himself, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Assurance is the British word for life insurance, so the second reading splits the answer into self plus assured.
explanation.definitionFit: A brash, overconfident person is sure of himself, which is exactly the everyday sense of this compound adjective.

clue.text: Ought Queen Elizabeth to love Francis B.? Cut!

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, shaped like the letter O
Francis Bacon the philosopher, playfully abbreviated the other way round as F. Bacon

explanation.surface: Should Elizabeth I fall for her courtier Francis Bacon? A director shouts that the scene is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis B. is Francis Bacon; the setter shortens his surname, and the solver must instead shorten his first name to F.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's cut is a joint of meat, and this joint from the pig's foreleg is one such piece.

clue.text: It's said to precede the quickest repair

definitions.text: It's said to precede the quickest repair

parts.words: It's said to precede the quickest repair
parts.note: surface reading: something reported to come before the fastest fix

parts.words: It's said to precede the quickest repair
parts.note: setter's reading: the word that comes before 'said' in the proverb ending 'soonest mended'

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Least said, soonest mended': quickest repair is soonest mended, and 'said' is a word in the proverb, not a hint about sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb's opening word stands directly before 'said', which is then followed by the phrase about quick mending.

clue.text: Opposition to the round church is somewhere in the Bible

explanation.surface: Objection to a circular church building, which is mentioned somewhere in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch is a city named in the Acts of the Apostles, where followers were first called Christians.

clue.text: Take a second to see 13, being tight

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
lo is an old word for look or see

explanation.surface: Take a moment to look at the garden building while being drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight and the answer are both informal British slang words meaning very drunk.

clue.text: Recover like a dog from the bulk of the River Tees

indicators.note: the bulk of something is most of it, so the final letter of the river's name is left behind

parts.note: the bulk of River Tees: all its letters but the last

explanation.surface: A dog fetches something out of most of the River Tees in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate anagram signal; the letters of River Tee are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gundogs called retrievers bring back shot game, so to recover something as a dog does is this verb.

clue.text: Computer reversion: like it to voice articles on 19?

parts.note: dig it is slang for like it
two indefinite articles, an and a
19-across is wood, and a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A computer going backwards: perhaps it gets to sing pieces on wood?
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the articles before the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting a computer's digital signal back to the older continuous kind is a going back, a reversion, in technology.

clue.text: The first proper American stove

explanation.surface: The original genuine American cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Primus is the brand of portable paraffin camping stove, and the Latin word for first, used in British schools for the eldest brother.

clue.text: A second off being clouded over: adverse condition to follow

indicators.note: 'off' as in taken off: the second is removed from the weather word

parts.note: with the sun hidden by cloud

explanation.surface: A weather report: briefly overcast, with something unfavourable on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: The conjunction introduces a condition that cuts against what came before: you'll go unless it rains.
explanation.definitionFit: This conjunction sets a negative proviso, introducing a requirement that comes after the main statement.

clue.text: Brazilian diplomacy may be taken as read when there's trouble

definitions.text: may be taken as read when there's trouble

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city

explanation.surface: Brazilian negotiators' diplomacy may be assumed known when trouble breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken as read' is an idiom for assumed, but here it is literal: the act was read aloud to disperse rioters.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the old British law, magistrates formally read this statute to a disorderly crowd before force could be used.

clue.text: Figure 0 on electronic device held by prisoner

parts.note: the digit zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: something held by a captor is gripped inside, so the device sits within the convict's letters

parts.note: an electronic tag worn by an offender

explanation.surface: A zero on an offender's ankle tag, worn by a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is an eight-sided shape, and in geometry a shape is called a figure.

clue.text: Kind to fairy that's out and fairy will be kind when I'm out!

definitions.text: Kind to fairy that's out and fairy will be kind when I'm out!

parts.words: Kind to fairy that's out and fairy will be kind when I'm out!
parts.note: surface reading: a riddle about kindness between fairies

parts.words: Kind to fairy that's out and fairy will be kind when I'm out!
parts.note: setter's reading: a child's first-set kind of tooth, which, once fallen out, earns a coin from the fairy

explanation.walkthrough: Kind means type: the answer names the kind of thing the tooth fairy collects.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's first teeth fall out naturally, and the tooth fairy leaves money under the pillow in exchange.

clue.text: See 14
See 19
Let initiative she'd held slip, as always at the 26 21

indicators.note: letting things slip lets them fall out of place, so the four words lose their order

parts.note: every letter of these four words

explanation.surface: She let the initiative she had held slip away, as so often in talks.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that problems hide in small particulars, which is what wrecks deals during talks.

clue.text: Scottish shepherd's hut is an improved English one

indicators.note: an improved version has been reworked, so the national word and numeral are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Highland herdsman's hut turns out to be an upgraded English version.
explanation.definitionFit: A shieling is a rough hut or shelter on summer pasture in Scotland, used by those herding sheep.

clue.text: Operator to gain entry for alternative worker in benefit

indicators.note: being in the benefit means sitting inside it, between its letters

parts.note: the dole is British unemployment benefit
a farm hand is a worker

explanation.surface: A con man gets into the welfare system by claiming as a replacement labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fitting you turn to open a door is literally the thing operated in order to get inside.

clue.text: See 14
Absence of saints among the upper aristocracy?

parts.note: the blest are the saints in heaven

explanation.surface: A wry observation that there are no saints in the highest ranks of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of noble describes those of the highest rank, the very top of the peerage.

clue.text: Young actress turning role model before Thanksgiving

indicators.note: a turning role is twisted around, so its four letters change order

parts.note: ta is British for thanks, so giving ta is giving thanks

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming actress changes her role-model ahead of the November holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Young is not about age: it is the surname of the Hollywood actress Loretta Young.
explanation.definitionFit: Loretta Young was an Oscar-winning Hollywood star, so the actress surnamed Young is identified by her first name.

clue.text: Bowl dropped where Ada Doom saw something nasty
Under Prohibition, without an audience, it's very boring

indicators.note: in the old sense, without means outside, so the prohibition word wraps around the hearing

parts.note: a dry country or state bans alcohol
to give someone an ear is to grant them a hearing

explanation.surface: Life during Prohibition, with no listeners around, was tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and tedious, dismal in a way that saps interest, is the sense shared by this adjective.

clue.text: See 26
Drink dispenser left pub — that's prison

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone left the barman and the pub behind, and ended up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Barlinnie is the large Victorian jail in Glasgow, Scotland's best-known prison.

clue.text: William (Bill) Shakespeare's feet

parts.note: William without its short form Will

explanation.surface: The feet of William Shakespeare, known as Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Both names are trimmed in parallel: William loses the nickname Will, and Bill loses the same ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote mostly in iambic pentameter, whose metrical units are these feet of one weak and one strong syllable.

clue.text: Slight gradient in cliff-top railway

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, so only the initial of the cliff counts

explanation.surface: A gentle slope on a funicular railway at the top of a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or rising surface, such as a hillside, is the noun sense of this word.

clue.text: Circus artist that can hold his drink?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an acrobat who does somersaults
second meaning: a drinking glass, which literally holds a drink

explanation.surface: Praise for an acrobat who doesn't get drunk easily.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performing flips is one sense; a flat-bottomed glass without a stem or handle is the other.

clue.text: Tyneside acquired one, with a feeling of excitement about the price: is it make of deal?

indicators.note: a feeling about something surrounds it, so the thrill's letters go round the cost

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England
a tab is a bill or price to pay

explanation.surface: A Geordie bought something, thrilled about its cost: is it made of pine?
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is pine wood, so a deal table is a pine one; but this table is where deals get made.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal talks are said to take place around this furniture, where opposing sides bargain to an agreement.
